guide.text:
# Replay concurrent-work ownership cases

> **In plain terms.** People and programs sharing one project can claim the same files, and someone must decide who owns each. This component is given made-up cases of who claimed which files, each claim marked live, stale or unknown. For each automatically generated file it ranks a live claim above an unknown or stale one, even when the stale one came first. It writes advice for each case, such as handing the file to its live owner, releasing stale claims or looking closer. That ranking step is checked by a mathematical proof against written rules.

`concurrency_mission_control` runs a copied mission-control builder against a temporary example directory. It then evaluates fixture cases about overlapping file claims, stale owners, deferred validation and commit status. The output is a JSON account of how those supplied cases are classified.

## Run the example

From the repository root, with Python 3.11 or later:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m microcosm_core.organs.concurrency_mission_control run \
  --input fixtures/first_wave/concurrency_mission_control/input \
  --out .microcosm/component-guides/concurrency_mission_control \
  --acceptance-out .microcosm/component-guides/concurrency_mission_control/acceptance.json
```

The result contains separate checks for the builder, transaction failure cases, provider-bridge records, claim ownership and closure status. Source-copy digests are checked before the exercise is accepted.

## What this checks

The classification functions derive their answers from the supplied owner and path records. A generated file with a live owner is assigned a handoff action, even if an earlier claim is stale. Release or replacement is advised when all matching claims are known stale; uncertain freshness calls for inspection. The closure classifier distinguishes completed validation from validation deferred because of host pressure. A missing seed root is rejected by the fixture. Tests alter ownership and path topology while leaving prewritten labels unchanged, checking that the computed classification changes.

## Limits

These are synthetic scenarios and copied-builder executions. The run does not coordinate currently running agents, acquire a lock in another repository or dispatch a provider job. A recommended action is a classification output, not enforcement against concurrent writers. The fixture therefore does not establish production concurrency safety.

## Verification

The generated-surface classifier calls the [proved ownership core](../formal/components/ownership_classification/README.md). For each normalized path it considers every matching claim, selecting a live claim ahead of uncertain or stale claims. The proof establishes that any matching live claim leads to a live-owner classification and handoff action. The host supplies the exact paths and freshness observations and reports the live representative; the proof does not establish actual liveness or enforce a lock.

The direct example uses that classifier. `make component-replays` separately applies the shared [replay admission check](../formal/replay/README.md) to the exported bundle.

## Sources

- [Implementation](../src/microcosm_core/organs/concurrency_mission_control.py), [exercise inputs](../fixtures/first_wave/concurrency_mission_control/input) and [tests](../tests/test_concurrency_mission_control.py).
- [Historical result](../receipts/first_wave/concurrency_mission_control/concurrency_mission_control_result.json) and [canonical description](../core/paper_module_capsules.json).

# Ownership classification core

`OwnershipClassification.dfy` proves that every matching live claim protects
its generated path, regardless of claim order. `Compute` returns a live-owner
classification and no-patch action whenever any generated path has a matching
live claim. `SelectedPrefix` independently specifies the earliest claim with
the highest observed priority: live, unresolved freshness, then stale.
Stale-release advice therefore requires that every matching claim is known
stale. This deliberately repairs the former first-matching-claim policy: an
earlier stale claim must not hide a later live owner.

The iterative `FindOwner` and `Compute` methods establish exact per-path
selection, the row partition, the aggregate priority and its corresponding
action code. Unknown observations receive a separate inspection action.
The first-claim mutant restores the old selection behavior without changing
the specification; a second mutant puts stale aggregate state before live.
Both fail their postconditions. `metadata.json` records the pinned compiler,
proof results, source-linked mutations and generated hashes.

The production generated-surface classifier calls this core through the sealed
component worker. Host normalization retains every supplied session-card and
claim freshness signal, protects any live signal, and treats missing owner
identity or otherwise uncertain freshness as unresolved. Reports retain all
matching claims and conflicting observations, flag distinct live sessions on
the same exact path, and select a live representative for a live handoff.
The closure lens uses that representative; its separate overbroad-scope case
also uses the same core selection policy.

The theorem concerns normalized exact path IDs and supplied freshness states.
Python normalization, representative display and collision diagnostics are
separately tested host operations. It does not prove session liveness,
identity authenticity, parent/child scope overlap, real lock enforcement or
concurrent execution safety. Boolean claim inputs remain compatible (`true`
means live and `false` means known stale); the host uses explicit
`live`/`unknown`/`stale` states. The compiler, Dafny runtime, Boogie/Z3,
adapter, sealed worker and host remain trusted. The worker has a 30-second
timeout and raises on failure without an unverified fallback; mathematical
termination does not establish a wall-clock or memory bound.

excerpts.name: SelectedPrefix
HasLive
RowSpec
excerpts.text:
predicate RowSpec(p: Path, claims: seq<Claim>, row: Row) {
    (!p.generated && row == Row(-1, 0)) ||
    (p.generated && SelectedPrefix(claims, p.id, |claims|, row.ownerIndex) &&
      ((row.ownerIndex == -1 && row.kind == 1) ||
       (0 <= row.ownerIndex < |claims| &&
        ((claims[row.ownerIndex].freshness == Live && row.kind == 2) ||
         (claims[row.ownerIndex].freshness == Unknown && row.kind == 5) ||
         (claims[row.ownerIndex].freshness == Stale && row.kind == 3)))))
  }

excerpts.name: ClassificationSpec
ActionSpec
FindOwner
LiveRowExact
excerpts.text:
lemma LiveRowExact(p: Path, claims: seq<Claim>, row: Row)
    requires RowSpec(p, claims, row)
    ensures row.kind == 2 <==> p.generated && HasLive(claims, p.id)
  {}
